LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mean_codebookOutp: Choose M ≥ 1 input words independently from q and transmit through the block channel K. With acceptance event A, the expected average decoding error is at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A), where J is the joint input–output law and S is the independent product of q with its induced output law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_mem_suppor: For M ≥ 1, some codebook in the support of M independent draws from q has average error through K, using the decoder for event A, at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A). Here J is the input–output joint law and S the product of its marginals.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_blockChann: For a finite memoryless channel, word law q, M ≥ 1 and event A, some supported codebook with the decoder for A has average error at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)S(A), where J is the joint law of the input word and output word and S the product of its marginals.

Let J be the joint law of an input word drawn from q and its output through Wⁿ, and S the independent product of its marginals. For any real t and M ≥ 1, some codebook in the support of M iid draws from q, using the decoder for A = {z : J(z) > exp(t)S(z)}, has average error at most J(Aᶜ) + (M−1)exp(−t).
